newsitem.title: USA: US spot jet fuel sizzles, buyers keep rally going.
newsitem.headline: US spot jet fuel sizzles, buyers keep rally going.

text.p: U.S. spot jet fuel prices streaked higher Wednesday as differentials continued their week-long rally on more refiner buying and a two-cent jump in February heating oil futures prices, traders said.
U.S. Gulf aviation-quality 54-grade fuel saw offers leap to 2.25 cents over the print late afternoon, 1.5 cents firmer than Tuesday diffs.

"There's no question they're stronger. It looks like a few people are caught short," one Gulf player said, noting today is the scheduling deadline for nominating front-third-cycle material for delivery on the Colonial Pipeline.
Gulf traders said Exxon, Koch Oil, Citgo and Conoco had all been seeking third-cycle 54-grade barrels earlier in the day.

Some players cited unconfirmed rumors of refinery output problems, while others ascribed growing differential strength to crimped supplies brought on by ongoing refinery maintenance turnarounds in the Gulf.
USG low-sulfur 55-grade diffs also firmed 1.5 cents, to 2.75 cents over the screen for front third-cycle material.
NYH 54-grade was talked as high as 5.0 cents over the print, a half cent firmer than Tuesday, while 55-grade saw diffs firm over one cent with deals done at 6.75 cents over, players said.
New York traders said diffs were buoyed by Gulf prices and reports that four jet fuel cargoes purchased last week were being loaded in the Gulf now for shipment to the West Coast.

"I don't think things will stay this high, it's not sustainable," one New York player said, cautioning that diffs -- which have firmed by about 2.5 cents during the past week -- could slide just as quickly.
((- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
